title: The secrets vault, from the owner to the family
promise: Maria keeps the passwords and account details her family will need in one encrypted place, mentions them where they matter, and decides who can open each one and when.

scenes.title: Everything in one encrypted place
scenes.proves: Settings → Secrets lists names only, each with who it is shared with.
scenes.watch: The list never carries a value; each row says if it is private, shared now or after death.

scenes.title: Shared on purpose
scenes.proves: A secret is added in a modal; sharing is an explicit choice, now or after her death.
scenes.watch: Required and optional fields are marked; sharing starts off.

scenes.title: A value, only when asked for
scenes.proves: Showing a value needs a recent second factor, hides itself, and every look is recorded.
scenes.watch: The session already passed the second factor; otherwise a code is asked first.

scenes.title: Mentioned right where it matters
scenes.proves: In an Important Note, typing @ lists her secrets and a click drops one into the text as a tag.
scenes.watch: The note keeps the name only; the value stays in the vault.

scenes.title: Her son sees what she chose
scenes.proves: A trusted contact allowed to see secrets gets only the ones shared with him now.
scenes.watch: The Wi-Fi is shared after her death, so it does not appear yet.

scenes.title: A tag is not a key
scenes.proves: A contact without the permission sees the mention's name in a note, and has nothing to open.
scenes.watch: No Secrets panel for Ana, and the API answers 404 to her for every secret.
